Sensitivity of the Estimate to Calibration Error

Source: R/sensitivity.R
drift_sensitivity.Rd

Bounds the bias of the soft_lm() estimate when the probabilities are miscalibrated given the controls by at most \(\delta\), and reports how much miscalibration the conclusion can tolerate.

Usage

drift_sensitivity(object, delta = NULL, level = 0.95)

# S3 method for class 'softcats_sensitivity'
print(x, digits = 3L, ...)

Arguments

object

[mandatory] (softcats) A fit returned by soft_lm().

delta

[optional] (numeric) Drift magnitude. If given, the bound and the intervals widened by the bound are added (default: NULL).

level

[optional] (numeric) Confidence level (default: 0.95).

x

[mandatory] (softcats_sensitivity) Result of drift_sensitivity().

digits

[optional] (integer) Number of significant digits to print (default: 3).

...

[optional] Not used.

Value

A data frame of class softcats_sensitivity with columns term, estimate, std.error, bias_per_delta, rv, rv_ci and, if delta is given, bound, conf.low and conf.high (the confidence interval widened by the bound on each side). The print method returns x invisibly.

Details

Suppose that the probabilities are miscalibrated given the controls, \(E[1\{G = k\} \mid p, X] = p_k + \eta_k(p, X)\) with \(|\eta_k| \le \delta\) for every category. Then the estimator of soft_lm() converges to \(\tau + M^{-1} E[a \eta^\top] \tau\) with \(M = E[a a^\top]\), and the bias of coefficient \(k\) is at most $$\delta \, \|\tau\|_1 \, E\left|(M^{-1} a)_k\right| .$$ For two categories this is \(|\tau| \, \delta \, E|a| / V^*\). drift_sensitivity() evaluates the factor multiplying \(\delta\) (the bias per unit of drift), using the estimate of \(\tau\), and reports two robustness values in the spirit of Cinelli and Hazlett (2020):

  • rv: the drift \(\delta\) at which the bound equals the absolute estimate. For two categories the bias is proportional to \(\tau\), so a drift below rv cannot reverse the sign of the effect;

  • rv_ci: the drift at which the bound equals the distance from zero to the end of the confidence interval nearest to zero, so that the interval widened by the bound includes zero.

The bound holds for every drift function within \(\pm\delta\) and is therefore conservative for any particular one. It is evaluated at the estimate of \(\tau\), so the widened interval summarises sensitivity and is not a confidence interval with guaranteed coverage. A value of \(\delta\) can be taken from calibration_check() (delta_hat).

References

Kurbucz, M. T. (2026). Coarsening latent-class probabilities: Directional distortion and coverage loss. arXiv preprint. doi:10.48550/arXiv.2608.11784

Cinelli, C. and Hazlett, C. (2020). Making sense of sensitivity: Extending omitted variable bias. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B, 82(1), 39–67. doi:10.1111/rssb.12348

Kurbucz, M. T. (2026). When to trust confidence thresholding: Calibration diagnostics for pseudo-labelled regression. arXiv preprint. doi:10.48550/arXiv.2605.12780

Examples

# Example: Robustness values and the bound at a drift of 0.02
d <- sim_softcats(n = 2000, K = 2, seed = 9)
fit <- soft_lm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, probs = d$prob_B, data = d,
               learner = lrn_lm(degree = 3), seed = 9)
drift_sensitivity(fit)
#> Sensitivity to calibration drift |eta| <= delta
#> 
#>  term estimate std.error bias_per_delta    rv rv_ci
#>     1    0.874    0.0748           2.44 0.359 0.298
#> 
#> bias_per_delta: largest bias per unit of drift.
#> rv: drift at which the bound equals the estimate.
#> rv_ci: drift at which the widened interval reaches zero.
drift_sensitivity(fit, delta = 0.02)
#> Sensitivity to calibration drift |eta| <= delta
#> 
#>  term estimate std.error bias_per_delta    rv rv_ci  bound conf.low conf.high
#>     1    0.874    0.0748           2.44 0.359 0.298 0.0488    0.679      1.07
#> 
#> bias_per_delta: largest bias per unit of drift.
#> rv: drift at which the bound equals the estimate.
#> rv_ci: drift at which the widened interval reaches zero.
#> Intervals are 95% confidence intervals widened by the bound at delta = 0.02.
